propositions: Manifest byte-equality tests flake under pytest-xdist when concurrent workers transiently modify the source checkout, causing git status --porcelain to report different dirty-state between separate build_manifest calls in one test.
The gate_code_version() function shells git status on every call, injecting non-deterministic -dirty suffixes into manifest signatures that should be stable within a single test.
Two manifest byte-equality tests compare outputs from separate build_manifest() calls without pinning the git provenance, allowing xdist workers to race and flip the -dirty flag between comparands.

The fix pattern—monkeypatching rebar.signing.gate_code_version to a constant—is already successfully used in test_no_pins_preserves_legacy_manifest_bytes and must be applied to test_manifest_file_scope_contract_preserves_legacy_bytes and test_manifest_is_deterministic_and_path_independent.
After pinning gate_code_version in all manifest byte-equality sites, the tests pass deterministically even when files are created in the checkout during test execution.
